purpose: Imported full pilot02 integrity audit and fit/cal model diagnosis; no new setting or checkpoint selection

inference.response_metric: Root mean square of normalized central differences of joint position/velocity; not radians or closed-loop tracking error
inference.q_metric: Open-loop joint-position RMSE averaged over +/- branches, blocks, 32 time steps and all 26 joints

conclusion.interpretation: C now matches B in cal joint-position prediction. Fit response RMSE8 improves, but cal RMSE8 is worse than same-iteration B at all four stored iterations for both seeds. This is consistent with response overfitting/generalization failure; it does not isolate the cause. Cal response32 also worsens, while response supervision covers only 8 steps and policy rollout still spans 32.

blockers: Fastest cal speed bin has only 4 blocks, below minimum 10
windows.warning: Diagnostic quantiles are not accepted tolerance settings; do not increase tolerance solely to produce long windows.

next_actions: Check finite-difference amplitude stability specifically on 4/8-step fit responses and compare CPU/GPU physics response under matched initial conditions before a new experiment.
Test a limited, matched B/C generalization intervention on fit/cal only; retain raw metrics and common forward data/normalization. Do not blindly extend the current training budget.
If source/config/data change, use a fresh attempt and protocol; preserve pilot01/pilot02 and their frozen inputs.
Resolve response validity, calibration coverage and an application-justified tolerance before D/C-perm; freeze final evaluation settings before locked test outcomes are inspected.
limitations: Two seeds and 200 iterations are pilot results, not converged policies or formal paper evidence
Training and calibration share no source sessions, but cal has already informed pilot02 configuration; these are development diagnostics, not an independent heldout validation
Independent hardware sessions and justified heldout actuator ranges remain unavailable
